options: a:The increased stopping distance the truck requires.,b:Decreased stopping distance for large vehicles.,c:Reduced noise levels from the truck.
note: Large vehicles need more stopping distance; remain visible to the truck driver and avoid lingering in blind spots.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When entering public traffic from a driveway or private road, what should you do regarding other drivers?
options: a:You have the right-of-way.,b:You may force your way into traffic.,c:Yield to drivers already on the public road.
note: Vehicles entering from driveways or private roads must yield to traffic already on the public road; merge only when it is safe.

question: Your vehicle's blind spot is the area:
options: a:You cannot see without turning your head.,b:You see in the rearview mirror.,c:Directly behind your vehicle only.
note: Blind spots are areas you can't see in mirrors and require a shoulder check to verify they are clear.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When two vehicles arrive at an unmarked intersection simultaneously, who has the right-of-way?
options: a:The vehicle approaching from the right.,b:The vehicle approaching from the left.,c:The vehicle that honks first.
note: At intersections of similar roads without control devices, yield to vehicles coming from your right.

question: If you notice a vehicle defect that could affect safe operation, what should you do?
options: a:Correct the defect when you can afford it.,b:Correct the defect as soon as possible.,c:Drive the vehicle at slower speeds until you can fix it.
note: Any defect affecting safe operation should be repaired promptly before driving the vehicle whenever possible.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you miss your exit on the freeway, what should you do?
options: a:Go to the next exit.,b:Make a U-turn through the median.,c:Pull onto the shoulder and back up to the exit.
note: If you miss an exit, continue to the next exit and re-route; do not stop, back up, or make unsafe turns on the freeway.

question: Does the type of alcoholic beverage change how significantly alcohol affects your reflexes and judgment?
options: a:No — any type of alcohol can impair reflexes and judgment depending on amount consumed.,b:Beer impairs much less than wine.,c:Hard ciders and mixed drinks are always worse.
note: Impairment depends on the amount of alcohol in the bloodstream, not the beverage type.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When may you cross double solid yellow lines?
options: a:To turn left into or out of a driveway or to make a permitted left turn.,b:To pass a slower vehicle.,c:To change lanes at any time.
note: Double solid yellow lines generally prohibit passing, but you may cross them to turn left into a driveway or highway or to make a permitted U-turn.

question: A stop sign is shaped like which of the following?
options: a:Rectangle.,b:Square.,c:Octagon.
note: Stop signs are octagonal and require drivers to come to a complete stop before proceeding when safe to do so.

question: When is it appropriate to use your horn?
options: a:To warn a pedestrian or driver of imminent danger, such as a child about to run into the street.,b:While travelling through an intersection to hurry traffic.,c:While passing a bicyclist at normal safe distance.
note: Your horn should be used as a warning to prevent a collision, for example if someone is about to step into your path unexpectedly.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When two vehicles reach an intersection at the same time from different highways, which vehicle must yield?
options: a:The vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right.,b:The vehicle on the right must yield to the vehicle on the left.,c:Both may proceed without yielding.
note: At simultaneous arrivals, the driver on the left yields to the driver on the right.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You must not drive your vehicle at a speed greater than:
options: a:A speed that is reasonable and prudent for conditions (and within legal limits).,b:The posted maximum speed only.,c:The minimum speed limit.
note: Drive no faster than is reasonable for current conditions; obey posted speed limits but slow when conditions require it.

question: On average, how quickly does the body eliminate alcohol?
options: a:About one standard drink per hour.,b:Three drinks per hour.,c:Two drinks per hour.
note: The average adult metabolizes roughly one standard alcoholic drink per hour, though many factors affect this rate.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: An advisory or restriction speed sign:
options: a:Has a triangular shape.,b:May be ignored in rainy, snowy, or icy conditions.,c:Is blue with black lettering.
note: Advisory speeds attached to warning signs indicate recommended speeds for those conditions; you must drive slower than posted advisory speeds when conditions are hazardous.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: While waiting in the intersection to complete a left turn, you should:
options: a:Signal and keep your wheels turned to the left.,b:Signal and keep your wheels straight.,c:Flash your headlights so drivers will let you through.
note: Keep your wheels pointed straight ahead while waiting to turn; that prevents being pushed into oncoming traffic if struck from behind.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When entering the street from a driveway, what must you do?
options: a:Must drive slowly to allow approaching vehicles and pedestrians time to get out of your way.,b:Must honk your horn so approaching vehicles and pedestrians know to give you room.,c:Stop and proceed only when there are no pedestrians or vehicles approaching.
note: Always come to a complete stop before entering the roadway from a driveway, yield to pedestrians and approaching traffic, and stop before crossing the sidewalk area.

question: Which factor(s) affect braking distance?
options: a:The speed your vehicle is traveling.,b:The condition of your brakes and tires.,c:All of the above.
note: Braking distance depends on speed, vehicle maintenance (brakes and tires), and pavement conditions; all these factors are important.

question: On a vertically arranged traffic light, what is the order of the lights from top to bottom?
options: a:Red, yellow, green.,b:Red, green, yellow.,c:Green, red, yellow.
note: A vertical traffic signal has red on top, yellow in the middle, and green on the bottom; horizontally it is red on the left and green on the right.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When parallel parking between two vehicles, what is the first positioning step?
options: a:Pull up even with the vehicle in front of the open space before backing in.,b:Turn your wheels to the right immediately.,c:Turn your wheels to the left immediately.
note: After signaling and checking traffic, stop even with the car ahead of the parking space, then begin backing into the spot.

question: What does a single broken white line between lanes indicate?
options: a:Lanes are moving in the same direction and drivers may change lanes when safe.,b:Lanes are moving in opposite directions and drivers may not pass.,c:Lanes are moving in the same direction and drivers are not permitted to pass.
note: A broken white line separates lanes moving in the same direction and indicates lane changes are permitted when it is safe to do so.

question: Which substances can impair driving and lead to DUII arrest?
options: a:Alcoholic beverages, controlled substances, and inhalants.,b:Only beer and wine.,c:Only prescription medicines.
note: Alcohol, illegal drugs, inhalants, and many legal prescriptions or OTC medications can impair driving and result in arrest.

question: Your vehicle's stopping distance increases when stopping:
options: a:When driving at night.,b:On a wet or icy road.,c:On paved highways.
note: Stopping distances are longer on wet, icy, or loose-surface roads; increase following distance in these conditions.

question: At a school crossing sign, what should you be prepared to do?
options: a:Always stop whether or not a stop sign is present.,b:Watch carefully for children and be ready to stop.,c:Always sound your horn when you see children.
note: When you see a school crossing sign, reduce speed and be alert for children; be prepared to stop even if no sign requires a full stop.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you miss your freeway exit, what is the correct action?
options: a:Continue to the next exit or location where you can safely turn around.,b:Back up on the shoulder to reach your exit.,c:Make the turn quickly from your current lane.
note: If you miss an exit, do not back up or make unsafe lane changes; proceed to the next exit and re-route safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you turn onto a two-lane road divided by a broken yellow line, you are on:
options: a:A two-way road.,b:A one-way road.,c:The road is under repair.
note: Yellow centerlines separate traffic moving in opposite directions; a broken yellow line means passing is permitted when safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which of the following should you do when preparing to change lanes?
options: a:Signal your intentions ahead of the lane change.,b:Rely solely on your mirrors.,c:Begin signaling as you move into the next lane.
note: Signal early to let other drivers know your intentions, check mirrors and blind spots, and ensure the lane is clear before changing.

question: A solid white edge line that angles toward the left means:
options: a:The roadway is narrowing ahead.,b:There is an intersection immediately ahead.,c:You will be required to turn left just ahead.
note: An edge line that slants toward the center indicates the road will become narrower.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When turning left, to whom must you yield the right-of-way?
options: a:Oncoming traffic and other road users already in the intersection.,b:Only to vehicles behind you.,c:Only to pedestrians who are off the curb.
note: Left-turning drivers must yield to oncoming vehicles and to pedestrians or other drivers already occupying the intersection.

question: When passing a large vehicle, what should the driver of a small vehicle be prepared for?
options: a:Wind gusts that can change the small vehicle's direction.,b:Loud music from the large vehicle.,c:Only visual obstructions, not wind effects.
note: Large trucks can create strong air turbulence; small vehicles should be ready to correct steering when passing or being passed.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At a four-way stop, who has the right-of-way?
options: a:The driver who arrived first.,b:The driver who arrived last.,c:The driver who does not stop.
note: At a four-way stop, the first vehicle to reach the intersection goes first. If two arrive together, the vehicle on the right has the right-of-way.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How should you use a freeway exit ramp correctly?
options: a:Keep your speed until you move onto the exit ramp, then slow.,b:Slow down before entering the ramp.,c:Maintain a constant speed while on the ramp.
note: Do not slow down on the freeway mainline; accelerate onto the ramp and then reduce speed after you are on it.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does a posted speed limit sign indicate?
options: a:The maximum safe driving speed under ideal road and weather conditions.,b:Only a suggested driving speed.,c:The exact speed you must drive to avoid a ticket in all circumstances.
note: A posted limit shows the maximum legal speed during ideal conditions; driving slower may be necessary for safety in poor conditions.

question: When borrowing an unfamiliar vehicle, what should you do before driving?
options: a:Familiarize yourself with controls like turn signals, lights, wipers, brakes, and horn.,b:Assume it's the same as your car and go immediately.,c:Hide defects to avoid embarrassing the owner.
note: Spend a few minutes locating and testing basic controls; fix any obvious defects before driving.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If an officer is directing traffic at an intersection, what should drivers follow?
options: a:The officer's directions instead of the traffic signal.,b:The traffic light's instructions.,c:Sound their horn to get attention.
note: Drivers, pedestrians, and cyclists must obey a traffic officer's directions even if they differ from the traffic signal.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You may legally pass on the right when:
options: a:Even if it means driving off the pavement.,b:On a narrow bridge.,c:If the vehicle ahead is waiting to turn left and there is an available passing lane.
note: You may pass on the right if the vehicle ahead is turning left and there is a safe, legal lane to pass in; you may never pass by driving off the pavement.

question: If a flagger is directing traffic in a construction zone, how should drivers respond?
options: a:Follow the directions given by the flagger.,b:Ignore the flagger and follow surrounding traffic.,c:Assume the flagger is not authorized to direct traffic.
note: Flaggers control traffic for safety in work zones; obey their directions, slow down, and exercise caution.

question: When it begins to rain while you are driving, you should:
options: a:Drive at the maximum posted speed limit.,b:Drive faster than surrounding traffic.,c:Slow down.
note: Reduce your speed, increase following distance, and turn on headlights in rain to improve visibility and traction.

question: 'Highway hypnosis' can result from:
options: a:Staring at the roadway for long periods without scanning.,b:Frequent rest stops.,c:Too much sleep the night before your trip.
note: Highway hypnosis is caused by prolonged, unvarying visual attention to the road; avoid it by periodically scanning and taking breaks.

question: What does a red and white triangular sign at an intersection indicate?
options: a:Always come to a full stop at the intersection.,b:Look both ways and be prepared to yield before entering the intersection.,c:Slow down if an emergency vehicle is approaching.
note: A red-and-white triangular sign is a yield sign: slow as you approach and yield the right-of-way to vehicles and pedestrians; be prepared to stop if necessary.

question: Larger vehicles compared with passenger cars have:
options: a:Larger blind spots.,b:No blind spots.,c:Smaller blind spots.
note: Trucks, buses, and large SUVs have bigger blind areas, especially close to the rear and sides, that mirrors may not show.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Who must yield when a driver is turning and a pedestrian is crossing without a traffic light?
options: a:The driver must yield to the pedestrian.,b:The pedestrian must yield.,c:Whoever started moving last must yield.
note: Drivers must yield to pedestrians crossing at intersections without traffic signals, even if no marked crosswalk exists.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How should you drive when passing through school zones?
options: a:Observe the posted speed limits and be prepared for increased enforcement.,b:Always travel no faster than 10 mph.,c:Expect students to yield to vehicles rather than you yielding to them.
note: Follow posted school zone limits and be especially watchful for children and crossing guards during school hours.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you want to turn left at an intersection with heavy oncoming traffic but the light is green, what should you do?
options: a:Enter the intersection to wait for a safe gap or use the next intersection.,b:Wait in the center of the intersection until traffic clears regardless of signal.,c:Turn immediately and force your turn.
note: You may move into the intersection to prepare for a left turn when the light is green, but do not block cross traffic; if unsafe, use the next intersection.

question: Is it legal to drink alcohol inside a vehicle on a public road?
options: a:No — consuming or possessing open alcoholic beverages on public roads is prohibited.,b:Yes, if you're not driving.,c:Yes, if you're in the back of a pickup.
note: Open alcoholic beverage consumption or possession in areas normally occupied by driver/passengers on public roads is illegal.

question: What should be your first response to reduced visibility?
options: a:Reduce your speed.,b:Turn on your windshield wipers.,c:Turn on headlights first.
note: Slow down first to match your speed to reduced visibility and hazardous conditions.

question: Why is maintaining a space cushion around your vehicle important?
options: a:It gives you time to react to unexpected situations.,b:It prevents distractions.,c:It keeps traffic flowing faster.
note: Leaving space around your vehicle provides reaction time for mistakes made by other drivers.

question: What is an effective way to help prevent crashes with other road users?
options: a:Communicate your intentions to other road users (signals, horn, lights) when appropriate.,b:Ignore other drivers and focus only on your vehicle.,c:Only drive on side streets to avoid traffic.
note: Communicating (signaling turns, brake lights, horn when needed) helps other road users predict your actions and reduces crashes.

question: What does a red arrow on a traffic signal require drivers to do?
options: a:Stop and remain stopped until a green light or green arrow appears.,b:Proceed slowly through the intersection.,c:Stop, then proceed when clear even if the red arrow is displayed.
note: A red arrow means you must come to a full stop and remain stopped until the signal changes to a green light or green arrow.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When approaching a railroad crossing without signals, you should:
options: a:All railroad crossings have signals so you will never encounter this situation.,b:Slow down and be prepared to stop.,c:Always bring the car to a complete stop.
note: Approach unprotected crossings with caution: slow down, look both ways, and be prepared to stop if you see or hear a train.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If your vehicle's turn signals stop working, you should indicate turns by using:
options: a:Your headlights,b:Hand signals,c:Your horn
note: If turn signals fail, use standard hand signals to show other drivers when you intend to turn or change lanes.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you're waiting to turn left at a multilane intersection but opposing traffic blocks your view, what should you do?
options: a:Wait until you can see all lanes you must cross before making the turn.,b:Accelerate quickly once the first lane is clear.,c:Wait for an oncoming driver to wave you across.
note: Do not begin a left turn until you can see that every lane you must cross is clear and you can turn safely.

question: How is drinking alcohol and then driving classified?
options: a:A minor traffic safety problem.,b:A serious traffic safety problem.,c:Safe if you have only had a few drinks.
note: Driving after drinking is a serious safety hazard: even small amounts of alcohol can impair judgment, coordination, and reaction time.

question: When driving in fog, you should use:
options: a:Your high beams.,b:Your parking lights.,c:Your low beam headlights.
note: Use low beam headlights (and fog lights if available) in fog, rain, or snow to reduce glare and improve visibility.

question: If your power steering fails while driving, how should you respond?
options: a:Work harder to steer, reduce speed, move to a safe location, and stop.,b:Turn on your hazard lights and immediately turn off the ignition.,c:Honk and keep driving normally until the car stops.
note: If power steering stops, steering will require more effort. Slow down, drive to a safe spot off the roadway, and stop the vehicle.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: From which lane should you begin a left turn on multilane one-way streets or highways?
options: a:The left lane.,b:The right lane.,c:The middle of the intersection.
note: When turning left on multilane one-way streets, start from the leftmost lane appropriate for the turn.

question: When approaching a stopped emergency vehicle with flashing lights, you must:
options: a:Change lanes away and slow down if possible; if not safe, slow below the posted limit and give extra room.,b:Stay in your lane and continue at speed.,c:Drive to the right and stop immediately in all cases.
note: If safe, move over; otherwise slow down below the speed limit and pass with caution, giving the stopped vehicle more space.

question: At dusk or on overcast days, which lights should you use?
options: a:Headlights (low beam).,b:Parking lights only.,c:No lights unless it rains.
note: Turn on your headlights at dusk or during overcast conditions and use low beams when other vehicles are within specified distances to reduce glare.

question: How should drivers adjust following distance in bad weather?
options: a:Increase their following distance.,b:Decrease their following distance.,c:Maintain the same distance as in good weather.
note: In adverse weather you need more time to stop, so increase your following distance to reduce crash risk.

question: If you are involved in a serious vehicle crash, what is your first required action?
options: a:Stop your vehicle at or near the scene.,b:Drive away to report it later.,c:Just call your insurance company without stopping.
note: If you are involved in a crash you must stop, move to a safe location if possible, check for injuries, and report it to law enforcement when required.

question: How does alcohol affect someone who drives after drinking?
options: a:They do not have sufficient control over their body, mind, or vehicle.,b:They are always aware of risks they are taking.,c:They become better drivers because they are more careful.
note: Alcohol impairs judgment, vision, concentration, and reaction time, reducing a driver's ability to operate a vehicle safely.

question: If your car starts to skid, which way should you turn the steering wheel?
options: a:In the opposite direction of the skid.,b:In the direction you want the vehicle to go.,c:To keep the front wheels straight.
note: If your vehicle skids, steer in the direction you want the vehicle to travel until it straightens out, then correct as needed.

question: What are signs called that require drivers to obey the instruction shown?
options: a:Regulatory signs.,b:Warning signs.,c:Information signs.
note: Regulatory signs indicate legal requirements (e.g., speed limits, no turns) and failing to obey them can result in penalties.

question: Which action best describes a defensive driver?
options: a:Anticipates the actions of other drivers and watches for hazards.,b:Drives slowly at all times.,c:Travels at a constant speed regardless of conditions.
note: Defensive drivers stay aware of surrounding traffic, anticipate potential problems, and take steps to avoid collisions.

question: How does cell phone use while driving affect safety?
options: a:It distracts drivers and can cause crashes.,b:It is not a problem in Idaho.,c:It is uncommon.
note: Using a phone while driving diverts attention; Idaho bans reading/writing/sending texts while driving (hands-free allowed).

question: Which of these does stopping distance NOT depend on?
options: a:Your own reaction time.,b:The time of day.,c:The condition of your vehicle's brakes.
note: Stopping distance depends on perception/reaction time, vehicle speed, vehicle weight, brake and tire conditions, roadway conditions, and weather—time of day is not a factor in physical stopping distance.

question: If your vehicle starts to skid, what is the correct response?
options: a:Turn your steering wheel in the direction of the skid.,b:Turn your steering wheel into oncoming traffic.,c:Overcorrect with quick steering movements.
note: If you skid, remain calm and steer gently in the direction the rear of the vehicle is sliding to regain control.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When moving from the right lane into the left lane on a multilane highway, you should:
options: a:Check mirrors and look over your left shoulder for vehicles in your blind spot, then signal.,b:Signal and turn immediately without checking behind.,c:Rely solely on side mirrors for clearance.
note: Always check mirrors and perform a shoulder check for the blind spot before changing lanes, and signal your maneuver.

question: If you are driving on a one-way street and an emergency vehicle using flashing lights approaches, you must:
options: a:Speed up and take the nearest exit.,b:Drive with your flashers turned on.,c:Drive toward the nearest roadside and stop.
note: On any street, pull to the nearest side of the roadway and stop to allow emergency vehicles to pass.

question: Regulatory traffic signs are usually which color and must be obeyed?
options: a:White,b:Blue,c:Green
note: Regulatory signs (such as speed limits and stop signs) are typically white with black or red markings and must be followed.

question: A single dashed white line between lanes indicates:
options: a:Drivers may not pass.,b:Lanes move in opposite directions.,c:Drivers may pass when it is safe to do so.
note: Broken white lines separate lanes moving in the same direction and may be crossed to pass or change lanes when safe.

question: Lanes of traffic moving in opposite directions are divided by what color lines?
options: a:Yellow lines.,b:White lines.,c:Black lines.
note: Yellow pavement markings separate traffic moving in opposite directions; white lines separate lanes moving the same direction.

question: When you drive through an area where children are playing, what should you expect?
options: a:They may run out in front of you without looking.,b:They will stop at the curb before crossing the street.,c:They will know when it is safe to cross the street.
note: Slow down and exercise extra caution near children; they may not recognize the danger and can run into streets without looking.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At an uncontrolled intersection where two vehicles arrive at the same time:
options: a:The largest vehicle has the right-of-way.,b:The car on the left has the right-of-way.,c:The car on the left shall yield to the car on the right.
note: When two vehicles arrive simultaneously at an uncontrolled intersection, the vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right.

question: The best way to reduce the risk of hydroplaning is to:
options: a:Keep your tires properly maintained.,b:Slow down when roads are wet or slushy.,c:Watch out for standing water or puddles.
note: Reduce speed on wet roads, avoid standing water, and maintain proper tire tread and pressure to minimize hydroplaning risk.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When should you begin to slow down while exiting a highway?
options: a:After you have moved into the exit lane.,b:On the main road before entering the exit lane.,c:Only when you see a toll booth.
note: Enter the exit lane in advance and then reduce speed once you are fully in the exit lane to avoid impeding traffic on the main roadway.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How can you avoid collisions caused by vehicles in your blind spots?
options: a:Quickly glance over your shoulder to check the blind spot before changing lanes.,b:Adjust rearview mirrors every few minutes instead of checking blind spots.,c:Honk immediately before changing lanes.
note: Always perform a quick over-the-shoulder check to verify the blind spot is clear before a lane change — mirrors alone may not show everything.

question: When you hear a siren or see flashing lights of an approaching emergency vehicle, what must you do?
options: a:Drive to the right side of the road and stop until the vehicle passes.,b:Slow down and continue at a reduced speed.,c:Motion to the emergency vehicle to pass on the left.
note: Yield the right-of-way to emergency vehicles by pulling to the right and stopping; if in an intersection, clear it first then pull over.

question: When approaching railroad tracks, what should you do?
options: a:Look, listen, slow down, and be prepared to stop.,b:Speed up to cross before gates lower.,c:Drive around a lowered gate.
note: Always look and listen for trains and be ready to stop; never try to go around lowered gates.

question: What does a diamond-shaped traffic sign indicate?
options: a:A warning about existing or possible hazards ahead.,b:A direction to the nearest city.,c:A regulation you must obey.
note: Diamond-shaped signs are warning signs, alerting drivers to upcoming conditions or hazards on the road.

question: At an uncontrolled railroad crossing without gates or flashing lights, what should you do?
options: a:Be prepared to yield to any oncoming train before crossing.,b:Always stop before crossing the tracks.,c:Cross the tracks immediately as quickly as possible.
note: Approach such crossings with caution, look and listen for trains, and do not proceed until you are sure the tracks are clear and there is room for your vehicle.

question: What steps should you take to cross railroad tracks safely?
options: a:Listen and look both ways, and proceed only when it is safe.,b:Cross quickly when you hear a train in the distance.,c:Only look both ways when the red light is flashing.
note: Always look and listen for approaching trains and be certain there is room to fully clear the tracks before you begin to cross.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What do speed limit signs indicate?
options: a:The maximum or minimum speed that is legally allowed under ideal conditions.,b:Potential driving speeds only.,c:The speed for heavy traffic only.
note: Speed limit signs show the legal maximum (or minimum) under ideal conditions; adjust speed downward when conditions warrant.

question: After stopping for a school bus that is unloading children, what should you watch for before proceeding?
options: a:Children walking along the side of the road.,b:Only the bus driver's signal.,c:Whether the children wave at you.
note: When a bus is loading or unloading, watch for children near the roadway or crossing; proceed only when safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When turning left from a two-way street onto a one-way street, where should your car end up?
options: a:In the left lane of the one-way street (closest to the lane you left).,b:In the right lane.,c:In the center of the street.
note: Complete the left turn into the lane closest to the lane you came from—typically the left lane on a one-way street.

question: If you're upset or angry after an incident at work, what is the safest thing to do before driving home?
options: a:Take a few minutes to calm down and collect yourself before driving.,b:Play loud music to drown out your thoughts.,c:Drive fast to let off steam.
note: Emotional distraction increases crash risk; take time to cool off so you can focus on driving safely.

question: What does a single broken yellow centerline on a two-lane road indicate?
options: a:Opposing traffic; passing is permitted when safe.,b:Opposing traffic; passing is prohibited.,c:Lanes moving in same direction only.
note: A dashed yellow centerline separates opposing traffic and allows passing when it is safe to do so.

question: If your vehicle's right wheels leave the pavement, what should you do?
options: a:Slow down, steer parallel to the road, and ease back onto the pavement when it is safe.,b:Stop quickly.,c:Accelerate and steer back onto the road quickly.
note: Do not panic. Take your foot off the accelerator, steer parallel to the roadway, slow down, and carefully ease back onto the paved surface when it is safe.

question: What do downward-facing triangular traffic signs generally indicate?
options: a:Drivers must yield.,b:School zones are ahead.,c:Construction work is present.
note: Inverted triangular signs typically indicate yield—wait for clear traffic or pedestrians before proceeding.

question: Does drinking coffee reduce your blood alcohol concentration (BAC)?
options: a:It decreases BAC.,b:It has no effect on BAC.,c:It cancels the alcohol's effects.
note: Coffee may make you more alert but does not lower BAC or sober you up.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You may pass another vehicle when:
options: a:By using the shoulder of the highway.,b:If your lane is next to a solid yellow line and the passing lane is clear ahead.,c:In a curve or on a hill because the chance is small that another vehicle is coming.
note: Passing on hills, curves, and on the shoulder is unsafe and illegal; only pass where it is permitted and safe to do so.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How should you respond to a 'Merging traffic' sign on the freeway?
options: a:Make room for entering vehicles; move over one lane if it is safe and clear.,b:Honk at incoming traffic to warn them.,c:Always remain at your present speed.
note: When you see merging traffic, adjust speed or change lanes when safe to allow a smooth merge and reduce congestion.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is required when you encounter a flashing red light at an intersection?
options: a:Come to a full stop, then proceed when it is safe.,b:Slow down and continue without stopping.,c:Proceed only when a green light appears.
note: A flashing red signal is treated like a stop sign — stop fully, yield, and go when the way is clear.

question: What lane width are motorcycles entitled to?
options: a:The same full lane width as other motor vehicles.,b:Half the width of a regular lane.,c:Only the bicycle lane.
note: Motorcycles are entitled to a full lane — they should be given the same space as any other vehicle.

question: Remember to signal when you:
options: a:Pull into traffic from a parking area or alley.,b:Pull into or out of a parking space.,c:Are changing lanes.
note: Always signal before making lane changes, pulling into traffic, or entering/exiting parking spaces so others know your intentions.

question: How can stress affect your driving?
options: a:It can reduce your ability to concentrate on driving.,b:It decreases your chances of an accident.,c:It causes you to fall asleep at the wheel.
note: Strong emotions—anger, fear, or excitement—can degrade concentration and driving performance; avoid driving while emotionally unstable.

question: Orange-colored road signs typically indicate:
options: a:School zone signs.,b:Work zone signs.,c:Regulatory signs.
note: Orange diamond-shaped signs with black lettering or symbols warn drivers of highway work zones and workers on or near the roadway.

question: If your car breaks down on a highway, what should you do to warn others and ensure safety?
options: a:Use your four-way flashers, move off the road, and lift your hood to indicate a disabled vehicle.,b:Sound your horn at passing motorists for help.,c:Stay in the middle of the road and wave cars around you.
note: When disabled on the highway, signal, move to a safe location off the road, use hazard flashers, and raise the hood to alert other drivers.

question: When must you pull over and stop for an emergency vehicle?
options: a:Whenever it is using lights or sirens, regardless of its direction of approach.,b:Only if it is following you.,c:Only if it approaches from the opposite direction.
note: You must pull to the right and stop for an emergency vehicle with lights or siren, whether it's approaching from behind or ahead.

question: What does the term \No zone\" refer to?"
options: a:The large blind spot areas around trucks and other large vehicles.,b:A designated no-passing zone on the roadway.,c:A one-way traffic area.
note: \No zones\" are truck and large-vehicle blind spots where smaller vehicles disappear from the driver’s view; avoid lingering there."

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At an uncontrolled intersection where you and a vehicle to your right arrive at the same time, what should you do?
options: a:Yield to the vehicle on your right.,b:Speed up to get through the intersection first.,c:Force the other vehicle to stop.
note: When two vehicles arrive at an uncontrolled intersection simultaneously, yield to the vehicle on your right and proceed when safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Where is passing prohibited?
options: a:Within 100 feet of an intersection.,b:On hills or curves where vision is restricted.,c:When approaching a stopped school bus that is loading or unloading passengers.
note: Passing is prohibited in numerous places such as within 100 feet of an intersection, on hills or curves where visibility is limited, and when a school bus has stopped to load/unload passengers.

question: When driving in rain, which headlights should you use?
options: a:Low beam headlights.,b:High beam headlights.,c:Parking lights.
note: Use low beams in rain, fog, and snow to avoid glare and to help others see you.

question: Distracted drivers have a higher crash risk when using which device?
options: a:CD player.,b:Radio.,c:Cell phone.
note: Cell phone use (including hands-free) is a major distraction and increases crash risk; any device that diverts attention is hazardous.

question: When you see other drivers acting angrily, you should:
options: a:Don’t make eye contact.,b:Distance yourself from the situation.,c:Don't react with hand gestures.
note: Avoid escalating incidents: do not make eye contact or gesture, and safely put distance between you and the angry driver.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you're stopped in line at a stop sign and there is no cross traffic after vehicles ahead pass, what must you do?
options: a:Come to a complete stop at the stop sign before proceeding.,b:Proceed without stopping again.,c:Slowly roll past the stop sign.
note: You must bring your vehicle to a full stop at the stop sign each time and yield before proceeding.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If two vehicles arrive at a four-way stop at the same time:
options: a:Drivers must make hand motions to communicate with each other.,b:The vehicle on the right has the right-of-way.,c:The vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right.
note: At a four-way stop, vehicles proceed in the order of arrival; if two arrive simultaneously, the vehicle on the left yields to the vehicle on the right.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: On a highway with double solid yellow center lines, when may you cross them?
options: a:You may cross to pass other vehicles if there is no oncoming traffic.,b:You may cross only to make a left turn into or from an alley, private road, or driveway.,c:You may never cross them under any circumstances.
note: Double solid yellow lines separate opposite directions of traffic and indicate no passing; crossing is allowed only to make a left turn into or from an alley, private road, or driveway.

question: You must try to notify the owner of a vehicle if:
options: a:You don’t like a bumper sticker displayed on their vehicle.,b:That they are breaking the law while talking on their cell phone while driving.,c:You hit their vehicle while it is unattended.
note: If you damage an unattended vehicle, make a reasonable effort to find the owner; if you cannot, leave your name, address, and license information in a note describing the crash.

question: Before switching on the ignition, what should you ensure about seat belts?
options: a:That you and all passengers have fastened their seat belts.,b:That only child passengers are buckled.,c:That only adult passengers are buckled.
note: Develop a routine of buckling your seat belt and ensuring all passengers are buckled before starting the vehicle.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You cannot pass safely on a two-way, two-lane street unless you:
options: a:Are able to clearly see the road ahead.,b:You can return to your lane before meeting oncoming traffic.,c:Your vehicle is capable of the speed necessary to pass.
note: Only pass when you can see clearly ahead, complete the pass before oncoming traffic arrives, and your vehicle can safely make the pass.

question: What is the most common cause of traffic crashes?
options: a:Bad weather,b:Human error,c:New drivers
note: Most collisions result from human error—drivers not seeing others or making unexpected mistakes—so communication and attention reduce crashes.

question: If your wheels drop off the pavement onto the shoulder, what should you do?
options: a:Slow down, control the steering, and carefully steer back onto the pavement when safe.,b:Brake hard and sharply turn back onto the pavement.,c:Stop immediately on the shoulder and wait.
note: If your wheels come off the pavement, gently reduce speed and when it is safe, steer gradually back onto the roadway without sudden movements.

question: If a transit vehicle is signaling to re-enter the main roadway after a stop, what should you do?
options: a:Honking to let them know you are there.,b:Move to the left lane without slowing.,c:Yield to the transit vehicle to allow safe reentry.
note: Yield to transit vehicles re-entering traffic after they stop to load or unload passengers; slow, change lanes, or stop as needed to allow safe reentry.

question: In which situation is it appropriate to sound your horn?
options: a:To warn others if they may not see you or if a collision seems likely.,b:To celebrate passing another car.,c:To signal a pedestrian to hurry across.
note: A horn should be used to warn others of danger, such as when you may collide with another vehicle or when a pedestrian is unaware of your approach.

question: What is the only reliable way to lower your blood alcohol concentration (BAC)?
options: a:Drink coffee.,b:Allow your body time to get rid of the alcohol.,c:Exercise.
note: Only time reduces BAC. Coffee, exercise, and fresh air do not speed up the elimination of alcohol from the body.

question: When approaching a steady red traffic light, what must drivers do?
options: a:Come to a complete stop and remain stopped until it is safe to proceed.,b:Continue driving if there is no cross traffic.,c:Slow down but roll through the intersection.
note: A steady red light requires a full stop; turning on red is allowed only where not prohibited and when safe to do so.

question: As a pedestrian, which behavior is safest?
options: a:Never enter a street or crosswalk when vehicles are approaching.,b:Always insist on the right-of-way over vehicles.,c:Enter a crosswalk at any time because vehicles must stop for you.
note: Even with crosswalk rights, pedestrians should not step into traffic when vehicles are too close to stop safely.

question: Roads can become very slick under which conditions?
options: a:When the temperature is below freezing,b:When it has just started raining,c:Both of the above
note: Roads are especially slippery at the start of rain (oil mixes with water) and when moisture freezes at temperatures below freezing.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What should drivers do when approaching a steady green traffic light?
options: a:Continue if the intersection is clear, but yield to pedestrians and vehicles already in the intersection.,b:Treat it like a four-way stop.,c:Stop if a police officer is nearby.
note: You may proceed on green but must yield to pedestrians in crosswalks and traffic already within the intersection.

question: If another driver is driving aggressively behind you, what should you do?
options: a:Try to get out of the aggressive driver’s way.,b:Stare at the driver as they pass.,c:Speed up as they are passing you.
note: Avoid confrontation: move safely out of the way, do not make eye contact, and do not respond aggressively.

question: When parking uphill on a street with a curb, turn your front wheels:
options: a:Turn your front wheels slightly to the right.,b:Turn your front wheels sharply toward the curb.,c:Turn your front wheels sharply away from the curb.
note: When parked uphill with a curb, turn your wheels away from the curb and apply the parking brake so the vehicle would roll into the curb if it moved.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When the centerline shows a solid yellow next to your lane and a broken yellow next to oncoming traffic, you may pass:
options: a:Only in an emergency.,b:If you are on an expressway.,c:If traffic is clear.
note: If the broken yellow line is on your side of center, you may pass when it is safe and there is no oncoming traffic.

question: As alcohol accumulates in your bloodstream, what happens to your driving skills?
options: a:Your reaction time slows and you make more errors.,b:You become less confident and more cautious.,c:Your body metabolizes alcohol faster to offset impairment.
note: Alcohol slows reflexes and judgment and increases overconfidence and errors; it does not speed up metabolism to compensate.

question: Which of these actions can help reduce road rage and aggressive driving?
options: a:Allowing extra travel time.,b:Using improper signals to hurry traffic.,c:Driving faster than the posted limit.
note: Planning ahead and allowing extra time reduces stress. Also follow speed limits and use proper signals to help prevent aggressive interactions.

question: Which combination of actions helps prevent hydroplaning?
options: a:Ensure tires have good tread depth and are properly inflated.,b:Ensure tires are underinflated to increase contact area.,c:All of the above (good tread, proper inflation, and reduced speed).
note: Good tread, correct tire pressure, and reducing speed in wet conditions all reduce the risk of hydroplaning.

question: What greatly increases stopping distances and crash severity?
options: a:Night drives,b:High speeds,c:Slow speeds
note: High speeds increase stopping distances and the severity of collisions; reduce speed to lower crash risk.

question: If you are taking an over-the-counter medication, what should you do before driving?
options: a:Read the label for warnings about operating a vehicle.,b:Drink alcohol instead to counteract the medicine.,c:Assume it is safe if it was not prescribed to you.
note: Many non-prescription drugs can impair driving; check labels and ask a pharmacist or doctor if you are unsure about effects.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: After stopping at a stop sign, what is the recommended scanning sequence?
options: a:Look left first, then right, then left again before proceeding.,b:Look right first, then left, then right again.,c:Only check your rearview mirror.
note: At a stop, look left first because vehicles from that direction may be closest; then check right and left again before moving.

question: Turning your head to check the blind spot before changing lanes is:
options: a:A bad driving habit.,b:A good driving habit.,c:Unnecessary if you have mirrors.
note: Looking over your shoulder to check blind spots is an important habit in addition to mirror checks before lane changes or merging.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What should you do when you approach an intersection with a flashing yellow light?
options: a:Slow down and proceed with care after checking for hazards.,b:Ignore it and proceed as usual.,c:Stop and wait for a green light.
note: A flashing yellow is a warning to slow and be prepared to yield or stop if necessary; proceed cautiously.

question: When should you increase your following distance?
options: a:When following a large vehicle that blocks your vision.,b:When exiting an expressway.,c:When following a motorcycle.
note: Increase following distance in many situations including when a large vehicle blocks your view, in bad weather, or when following motorcycles or bicycles.

question: When traveling to an unfamiliar area, what is the best practice?
options: a:Should depend on road signs to find your way.,b:Plan your trip in advance.,c:Only have to know generally where your destination is.
note: Plan your route before you drive to an unfamiliar area; don’t rely solely on vague directions or on-the-fly decisions.

question: Which of the following is true about seat belts and child restraints?
options: a:You should never place an infant or small child in the front seat of a vehicle with airbags.,b:Airbags are always safe for infants.,c:Children 12 and under should always ride properly restrained in the rear seat.
note: Infants and small children should ride in proper child restraints in the back seat; a rear-facing infant seat should never be placed in the front seat of a vehicle with a passenger airbag.

question: To check blind spots when changing lanes you should:
options: a:Using the outside rearview mirror.,b:Using both inside and outside rearview mirrors.,c:Using the inside rearview mirror.
note: Always look over your shoulder to check blind spots in addition to using mirrors before changing lanes.

question: What can happen when alcohol is combined with drugs?
options: a:The effects of both may increase, making driving more dangerous.,b:It decreases both effects.,c:It cures the illness.
note: Mixing alcohol with drugs can amplify impairment and greatly increase the danger of driving.

question: How must you respond when an emergency vehicle approaches using sirens and/or flashing lights?
options: a:Pull to the right and stop immediately.,b:Pull to the right and slow down but keep moving.,c:Turn on your vehicle's four-way flashers and continue at the same speed.
note: When an emergency vehicle is approaching with warning signals, move to the right side of the road and stop to allow it to pass safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When turning left onto a one-way street, you should complete the turn into:
options: a:Either lane.,b:The lane closest to your previous lane.,c:The right lane.
note: When turning onto a one-way street, turn into the lane nearest your original lane unless signs or markings direct otherwise.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a driver's left arm and hand are extended upward, what is the meaning of this hand signal?
options: a:The driver intends to turn right.,b:The driver intends to turn left.,c:The driver intends to stop.
note: A left arm extended upward is the traditional hand signal indicating a right turn.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When merging onto a highway from an entrance ramp, what should you generally do?
options: a:Accelerate to match the speed of traffic and merge into a gap.,b:Stop at the end of the ramp then enter slowly.,c:Enter above the speed of traffic to get ahead.
note: Use the acceleration lane to reach the speed of highway traffic, signal, find a gap, and merge smoothly without forcing other drivers to change speed.

question: Which of the following will limit your concentration, perception, judgment, and memory?
options: a:Only a blood alcohol level greater than the legal limit can.,b:Alcohol does not affect those abilities.,c:Even the smallest amount of alcohol can.
note: Even small quantities of alcohol impair concentration, perception, judgment, and memory; no amount of alcohol is safe before driving.

question: If you need to slow down on a slippery road, what is the first step?
options: a:Take your foot off the gas pedal.,b:Firmly apply the brakes.,c:Apply the parking brake.
note: First ease off the accelerator to reduce speed; then gently apply brakes if additional slowing is needed.

question: If you have been drinking socially, what practice helps ensure a safe trip home?
options: a:Ride home with a friend who has not been drinking.,b:Drink coffee before driving.,c:Take a cold shower before driving.
note: Arranging a sober ride home prevents impaired driving; caffeine or showers do not reduce blood alcohol concentration.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Before passing another vehicle you should:
options: a:Honk your horn at least three times.,b:Re-enter your lane within 10 feet of the passed vehicle.,c:Check your mirrors and blind spots.
note: Before passing, check mirrors, signal, and look over your shoulder to check the blind spot; return to your lane only when it is safe.

question: What risks do worn or bald tires present?
options: a:They can increase your stopping distance and make turning more difficult.,b:They improve fuel economy.,c:They reduce the risk of hydroplaning.
note: Worn tires reduce traction, increasing stopping distance, making steering less effective, and raising hydroplaning risk.

question: When are you not required to stop for a stopped school bus?
options: a:When traveling in the opposite direction on a roadway with four or more lanes.,b:When driving on a two-lane road in the opposite direction.,c:When the bus is unloading on your same side.
note: On multi-lane highways with two or more lanes in each direction, oncoming traffic is not required to stop for a school bus that is stopped with its stop arm out.

question: At night, which road user is typically the hardest to see?
options: a:Pedestrians,b:Road signs,c:Other motorists
note: Pedestrians can be the hardest to detect at night because they are smaller and may not be well-lit or wearing reflective clothing.

question: When roads are slippery, what should you do to reduce crash risk?
options: a:Increase your following distance.,b:Drive the same as on dry roads.,c:Use alternate routes regardless of conditions.
note: Slippery conditions increase stopping distances, so add extra space between vehicles to compensate.

question: When you see a railroad crossing warning sign, what should you be prepared to do?
options: a:Stop if a train is nearby.,b:Drive faster than the train.,c:Look for a way around any lowered gates.
note: Railroad warning signs indicate a track ahead; be ready to stop if you see or hear an approaching train and obey all signals.

question: Look over your shoulder to check blind spots when:
options: a:Turning left or right.,b:Pulling toward or away from a curb.,c:Changing lanes.
note: Check blind spots by looking over your shoulder whenever you change lanes, turn, or move toward/away from the curb.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the correct behavior for a vehicle entering interstate traffic from an entrance ramp?
options: a:Yield to drivers already on the interstate.,b:Force their way into traffic.,c:Assume they have the right-of-way.
note: Vehicles entering from acceleration lanes should yield to highway traffic and merge when a safe gap appears.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At an intersection with a yield sign, what is required of you?
options: a:Always come to a complete stop before entering.,b:Yield the right-of-way to traffic in the intersection or roadway you are entering.,c:Yield only to traffic on your left.
note: A yield sign requires slowing and yielding the right-of-way to traffic and pedestrians already in the intersection or lane you are entering; stop if necessary.

question: If an oncoming driver fails to dim high beams, where should you look?
options: a:Toward the right side of the road.,b:At the approaching vehicle's wheels.,c:Directly into the lights.
note: Glance toward the right edge of the road to avoid being blinded while maintaining enough view of the roadway.

question: What types of drugs can impair your driving?
options: a:Prescription, over-the-counter, and illegal drugs.,b:Only illegal drugs.,c:Only allergy medicine.
note: Many medications—prescription, OTC, and illegal—can impair driving; always check side effects before driving.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Before making a left turn, what must you do?
options: a:Yield to oncoming vehicles and pedestrians.,b:Sound your horn.,c:Swing to the right side of your lane.
note: When turning left, yield the right-of-way to oncoming traffic and pedestrians before completing your turn.

question: The safest way to drive through a curve is to:
options: a:Maintain a constant speed throughout the curve.,b:Slow down as you enter, speed up as you exit.,c:Speed up as you enter, slow down as you exit.
note: Reduce speed before entering a curve and gradually accelerate as you exit to maintain control of the vehicle.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When a traffic light changes from green to solid yellow as you approach, you should:
options: a:Consider it the same as a caution sign and continue through the intersection.,b:Stop immediately.,c:Stop before entering the intersection unless you are too close to stop safely.
note: A steady yellow light means the signal is about to turn red; stop if it is safe to do so, but if you are too close, proceed with caution.

question: Which factors influence blood alcohol concentration (BAC)?
options: a:Amount of food in your stomach, your body weight, and time between drinks (all influence BAC).,b:Only the type of alcoholic beverage.,c:Only how much you weigh.
note: BAC depends on how much alcohol you drink, how long it is consumed over, and body weight; food can slow absorption but not prevent intoxication.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When are drivers required to stop their vehicle?
options: a:At stop signs, red lights, or when ordered by a traffic officer.,b:Only at stop signs.,c:Only when a red light is flashing.
note: You must stop at stop signs, at red or flashing red lights, and whenever a traffic officer directs you to stop.

question: What does an 'End school zone' sign indicate?
options: a:The reduced school speed limit has ended.,b:That the speed limit is 20 mph.,c:The increased possibility of encountering pedestrians.
note: An 'End school zone' sign indicates the end of the reduced school speed zone; resume the posted regular speed limit unless otherwise indicated.

question: What do regulatory traffic signs communicate?
options: a:They indicate what drivers must or must not do.,b:They warn of hazardous conditions.,c:They are diamond-shaped and yellow or green.
note: Regulatory signs (often rectangular, white with black markings) tell drivers required or prohibited actions, like speed limits or turn restrictions.

question: On slick roads, you should:
options: a:Accelerate quickly.,b:Change lanes quickly.,c:Take turns more slowly than usual.
note: When roads are slippery, reduce speed, brake and steer smoothly, and take turns more slowly than you would in dry conditions to avoid skidding.

question: What does a regulatory sign with a red circle and diagonal slash indicate?
options: a:The specified action is prohibited.,b:Drivers must come to a complete stop.,c:Some drivers must yield to others.
note: A red circle with a slash across a black symbol means the depicted action (e.g., no left turn) is forbidden.

question: Pennant-shaped signs are used to indicate:
options: a:No passing zones.,b:School zones.,c:Speed limits.
note: A pennant-shaped sign on the left side of the roadway warns drivers of a no-passing zone.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If an intersection is blocked by other traffic, you should:
options: a:Get as close as possible to the car in front of you.,b:Go slowly until the traffic ahead moves.,c:Stay out of the intersection until you can pass through.
note: Do not enter an intersection unless you can clear it; blocking an intersection impedes traffic and can be illegal.

question: When you first get into a car, what should you adjust first if needed?
options: a:Your seat so you can reach controls and see clearly.,b:Your seat belt.,c:Your rearview mirror.
note: Adjust your seat first so you can reach the pedals and controls comfortably and have a clear view; then adjust mirrors and steering column.

question: When backing up, what is the recommended way to check for hazards?
options: a:Turn your head and look through the rear window while backing.,b:Rely only on your mirrors.,c:Open your door to check behind you.
note: When reversing, physically turn and look over your shoulder through the rear window; do not depend solely on mirrors or sensors.

question: How can you help prevent rear-end collisions?
options: a:Avoid sudden stops by releasing the gas to slow, then apply steady brake pressure.,b:Pump your brakes rapidly before stopping.,c:Stop abruptly to warn drivers behind you.
note: Prevent rear-end crashes by signaling, gradually reducing speed, and applying brakes smoothly to give drivers behind time to react.

question: A steady yellow traffic signal means which light will appear next?
options: a:Steady red.,b:Flashing yellow.,c:Steady green.
note: A steady yellow warns that the signal is about to change to red; prepare to stop unless it is unsafe to do so.

question: Which rule applies to bicyclists in Idaho regarding stop signs?
options: a:Bicyclists are not required to always come to a complete stop at stop signs but must yield to vehicles already at the intersection.,b:Bicyclists must always come to a full stop at stop signs.,c:Bicyclists must stay off sidewalks.
note: Idaho allows bicyclists to treat some stop signs as yield signs but they must yield to vehicles and proceed with caution.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A flashing red light corresponds with:
options: a:A solid green light.,b:A flashing yellow light.,c:A solid red light.
note: A flashing red light functions like a stop sign: come to a complete stop, yield, and proceed when safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When is it illegal to pass another vehicle on the right?
options: a:You are on a multilane highway and the vehicle you are overtaking is driving below the speed limit.,b:You are on a two-lane, one-way road and the vehicle you are overtaking has stalled.,c:The vehicle you are overtaking is driving below the speed limit and you must use the shoulder of the road to pass.
note: You may not leave the main-traveled portion of the road (use the shoulder) to pass; passing on the right by using the shoulder is illegal.

question: An inattentive driver is one who:
options: a:Stares at objects off the roadway or daydreams while driving.,b:Maintains eye contact during conversation with a passenger.,c:Only watches the vehicle ahead of them.
note: Distractions such as daydreaming, looking away from the road, or interacting with passengers reduce awareness and increase crash risk.

question: If your vehicle's accelerator sticks while driving, you should:
options: a:Blow your horn.,b:Turn on your four-way flashers.,c:Slam on your brakes.
note: If the accelerator sticks, shift to neutral and turn off the ignition when safe, apply the brakes carefully, turn on hazard lights, and steer off the road.

question: When approaching a railroad crossing with flashing signals, what is the correct action?
options: a:Stop at least 15 feet from the nearest rail and look for a train.,b:Slow down and creep across the tracks.,c:Speed up and cross before the train arrives.
note: If warning lights are flashing, you must stop your vehicle at a safe distance (typically no closer than 15 feet) and wait until it is safe to proceed.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you are driving so slowly that traffic is backing up behind you, what should you do?
options: a:Pull off to the right and let traffic pass when safe to do so.,b:Continue at the same slow speed regardless of backups.,c:Refuse to let following cars pass by blocking them.
note: If you are impeding traffic by driving very slowly, safely pull off the road to allow vehicles to pass.

question: Traffic signs and pavement markings must be:
options: a:Merely suggestions.,b:Always obeyed.,c:Followed only when other traffic is present.
note: Traffic signs, signals, and pavement markings control flow and safety on the roadway and must be obeyed.

question: Why must drivers be extra alert for motorcyclists, bicyclists, and pedestrians?
options: a:They can be harder to see and notice in traffic than other vehicles.,b:They always follow different traffic laws.,c:They always have the right-of-way.
note: Smaller road users are more difficult to see, may be less visible at night or in traffic, and can move unpredictably, so stay alert for them.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the proper way to enter a freeway?
options: a:Signal, yield to freeway traffic, and accelerate to match the flow before merging.,b:Enter slowly; freeway traffic must yield to you.,c:Stop on the ramp to judge traffic and then enter.
note: When merging, signal, yield to existing traffic, and enter at a speed that matches traffic to merge safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When preparing to turn left, drivers should:
options: a:Slow down gradually while checking mirrors and signal in advance.,b:Expect pedestrians to yield to them.,c:Proceed quickly because they have the right-of-way.
note: Signal several seconds before turning, check mirrors, reduce speed, yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians, and complete the turn when safe.

question: Where are stop lines (solid white lines) painted on the roadway?
options: a:At intersections and pedestrian crosswalks.,b:Only on hills and curves.,c:Next to churches and schools.
note: Stop lines mark exactly where you must stop at intersections or crosswalks and are painted across traffic lanes.

question: About half of all motorcycle crashes involve what?
options: a:Another motor vehicle.,b:Bad weather.,c:Only minor injuries with no fatalities.
note: Approximately one-half of motorcycle collisions involve another motor vehicle, so be particularly vigilant for motorcycles around you.

question: What type of signs warn drivers about hazardous conditions ahead?
options: a:Warning signs (typically yellow and diamond-shaped).,b:Regulatory signs.,c:Information signs.
note: Warning signs alert drivers to potentially hazardous conditions; obey them to reduce accident risk.

question: Where should pedestrians yield to motor vehicles?
options: a:When crossing where there is no crosswalk or intersection.,b:When crossing at a marked crosswalk.,c:When the motor vehicle is a pickup truck.
note: Pedestrians must yield to vehicles when crossing mid-block or where no crosswalk exists; otherwise drivers must yield at marked crossings.

question: You may pass another vehicle if the dividing line between lanes is which type?
options: a:Broken white line.,b:Solid yellow line.,c:Double solid yellow line.
note: Broken white lines separate lanes moving in the same direction and may be crossed to pass when safe.

question: On a road without sidewalks, where should a pedestrian walk?
options: a:On the side of the road facing oncoming traffic.,b:On the same side and direction as traffic.,c:On the side with the lightest traffic.
note: Pedestrians should walk facing traffic so they can see oncoming vehicles and make eye contact with drivers when possible.

question: If your vehicle lacks ABS and you must stop quickly, what should you do?
options: a:Firmly pump your brakes.,b:Hold the brake pedal down continuously.,c:Lightly tap the brakes.
note: On vehicles without ABS, pumping the brake pedal helps bring the vehicle to a quick stop while maintaining steering control.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Under what condition may you pass another vehicle within an intersection in Idaho?
options: a:If a dashed yellow pavement marking continues through the intersection.,b:Under no circumstances.,c:If a dashed and a solid yellow line are marked through the intersection.
note: If the dashed yellow centerline continues across an intersection, passing may be allowed; if the line is solid at the intersection, passing is prohibited.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you miss your interstate exit, what should you do?
options: a:Get off at the next exit and return to the missed exit.,b:Stop and make a U-turn on the highway.,c:Ask another driver for help through your window.
note: Never back up or turn around on the highway; take the next exit and safely come back to your destination.

question: If you must drive in fog, which lights should you use?
options: a:Low-beam headlights.,b:Hazard lights only.,c:High-beam headlights.
note: Use low beams in fog; high beams reflect off the fog and reduce visibility further.

question: What is the usual effect of being distracted while driving?
options: a:It causes the driver to react more slowly to hazards.,b:It makes drivers drive faster.,c:It always improves driver awareness.
note: Distracted driving slows reactions and reduces attention to hazards, increasing the likelihood of collisions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Signaling your intentions before turning or changing lanes is:
options: a:A good driving habit and is required by law.,b:Necessary only if other traffic is present.,c:Necessary only during the maneuver, not before.
note: You must signal in advance (at least 100 feet where applicable) before turning, changing lanes, or pulling away from a curb so other road users can anticipate your actions.

question: What does a 'Reduced speed, 35 mph' sign mean when you encounter it?
options: a:The new 35 mph speed limit starts at that sign.,b:The new 35 mph limit begins at the next speed limit sign.,c:You have plenty of time to decelerate before the reduced speed zone.
note: A posted 'Reduced speed' sign establishes the new speed limit beginning at the sign; slow to the posted speed as you reach it.

question: Which of the following is NOT an effect of drinking alcohol?
options: a:Your reflexes and reaction time slow down.,b:Your judgment of speed and distance is distorted.,c:You become more alert.
note: Alcohol impairs reaction time and judgment and reduces alertness. Claiming it makes you more alert is incorrect.

question: If you are worried, nervous, angry, or crying before driving, what should you do?
options: a:Drive immediately because emotions won’t affect you.,b:Take time to calm down and focus before starting the engine.,c:Drive faster because you are more alert.
note: Emotions can distract your attention and reduce driving ability; calm down and refocus before driving.

question: During a tire blowout, what is the correct sequence of actions?
options: a:Take your foot off the accelerator, do not brake immediately, gradually slow and pull off the road.,b:Slam on the brakes immediately to stop quickly.,c:Accelerate to maintain control then pull over.
note: If a tire blows, ease off the gas, avoid sudden braking, slow gradually, steer straight, and pull off the roadway when safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A flashing red traffic signal at an intersection requires you to do what?
options: a:Stop and treat the intersection like a stop sign, then proceed when safe.,b:Slow down and proceed without stopping.,c:Yield to traffic only from the left.
note: A flashing red signal means stop completely; proceed only after yielding to other traffic and pedestrians.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When is driving below the speed limit illegal?
options: a:When driving slowly disrupts the normal traffic flow.,b:Only in rural areas.,c:When in heavy construction traffic.
note: It's unlawful to drive so slowly that you impede normal traffic flow; you may be cited for driving too slowly.

question: What is the most important thing to remember about speed management in curves?
options: a:Slow down before you enter the curve.,b:Maintain posted speed and slow at the sharpest part.,c:Accelerate gently into the curve.
note: Reduce speed before entering a curve; inertia can push you outward and make control difficult if you slow too late.

question: If it begins to sleet or snow while you are driving, what should you do?
options: a:Keep windshield and mirrors clear and increase following distance.,b:Approach all vehicles with caution.,c:Drive faster to get out of bad weather.
note: In snow or sleet keep windows and mirrors clear and increase the distance between you and other vehicles, since stopping distances increase on slippery surfaces.

question: When a traffic signal turns green, what should you do first?
options: a:Yield the right-of-way to pedestrians and any traffic still in the intersection.,b:Accelerate as quickly as possible.,c:Back up slowly.
note: A green light permits you to go, but first yield to pedestrians and any vehicles that remain in the intersection.

question: Which of the following is true about passing motorcycles?
options: a:The driver of a passenger vehicle must change lanes completely when passing a motorcycle.,b:A motorcycle with two people on it is more balanced than a motorcycle with just one rider.,c:It is okay for drivers of other vehicles to follow motorcycles closely.
note: Motorcycles are entitled to the full width of a lane; when passing a motorcycle you must move fully into the adjacent lane if available.

question: What color background do guide/destination signs have?
options: a:Green.,b:Yellow.,c:Red.
note: Guide signs that provide destinations and mileage information are green with white letters and symbols.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you must stop at an intersection with no stop line or crosswalk markings, you should:
options: a:Stop only at a place where they can see at least 200 feet on either side, even if they have to enter the intersecting roadway.,b:Is not required to stop.,c:Is required to slow down to make sure crossing traffic is clear.
note: Where no stop line or crosswalk is present, stop at the point nearest the intersecting roadway where you can see approaching traffic without entering it.

question: Where is it important to slow down?
options: a:On narrow or winding roads, at intersections or railroad crossings, and when roads are slippery.,b:Only on steep hills.,c:Only when pedestrians are present.
note: Reduce speed on narrow/winding roads, intersections, railroad crossings, hills, blind curves, and wet/slippery conditions to maintain control.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does a steady yellow traffic light indicate?
options: a:Slow down and prepare to stop; a red light will soon appear.,b:Proceed without stopping.,c:Stop immediately only if there are vehicles to your left.
note: A steady yellow warns the signal is about to turn red; slow down and stop if it is safe to do so.

question: Always use signals when:
options: a:Pulling into traffic from an alley or parking area.,b:Pulling into or out of a parking space.,c:Changing lanes.
note: Use turn signals when changing lanes, entering traffic from a parking area or alley, or pulling into/out of a parking space to communicate your intentions to others.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When approaching an uncontrolled intersection, a driver should:
options: a:Yield to all other drivers.,b:Stop at the intersection, check in all directions, and proceed.,c:Maintain their speed and proceed.
note: At intersections without signs or signals, slow, cover the brake, look left-right-left, and yield to vehicles on your right when required.

question: You can avoid alcohol-related crash risk by:
options: a:Calling a taxi.,b:Simply saying - No thanks I'm driving if someone offers you a drink.,c:Deciding before you start drinking that you are not going to drive.
note: The safest option is to decide before you start drinking that you will not drive; have a designated driver or alternative transportation.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When making a right turn on a green light, what must you do?
options: a:Yield to pedestrians and other traffic in the intersection before turning.,b:Maintain your normal speed without yielding.,c:Stop and look for police cars first.
note: Unless prohibited by a sign, you may turn on green but must yield to pedestrians and vehicles already in the intersection.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When approaching a slow-moving heavy truck from behind on a hill, what should you expect?
options: a:The truck may be traveling slower than the posted speed limit.,b:You are always able and allowed to pass the truck safely.,c:The truck must move over for you.
note: Large vehicles often slow on inclines; be cautious and only pass when it is legal and safe to do so.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When merging onto a freeway, what is usually best practice?
options: a:Accelerate on the ramp to match traffic speed and blend in safely.,b:Proceed slowly and wait for a special opening.,c:Turn on your hazard lights until merged.
note: Use the acceleration lane to reach freeway speeds and merge smoothly with traffic; entering traffic must yield.

question: Where should you try to maintain a space cushion around your vehicle?
options: a:On all sides of your vehicle.,b:Only in back of your vehicle.,c:Only on the left and right sides.
note: Maintain space in front, behind, and to both sides so you have room to maneuver and time to react to hazards.

question: If a green arrow changes to a solid green light, you:
options: a:Still have the right-of-way to turn.,b:May no longer turn and must proceed straight.,c:May still turn, but you must yield to oncoming traffic.
note: When the green arrow ends and a solid green is displayed, you may still turn but must yield to oncoming vehicles and pedestrians.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You must stop at a railroad crossing when:
options: a:Flashing red signals and gates are present and operating.,b:Directed to do so by a flagger.,c:It is controlled by a stop sign.
note: You must stop at a railroad crossing when directed by a flagger, a stop sign, or when warning devices (lights/gates) indicate a train is approaching.

question: What can happen if you drink alcohol while taking prescription or over-the-counter medication?
options: a:The combination could multiply the effects of the alcohol or medicine.,b:The medicine reduces the effect of the alcohol.,c:The alcohol will help the medicine cure a cold.
note: Alcohol can interact with many medications to increase impairment; combining drugs and alcohol can multiply effects and increase risk.

question: When parking uphill next to a curb, you should:
options: a:Keep the front tires straight ahead.,b:Keep the rear tires against the curb.,c:Turn your steering wheel away from the curb.
note: On an uphill with a curb, set the parking brake and turn the wheels away from the curb so if the vehicle rolls it will roll into the curb.

question: What can occur when alcohol is combined with another drug?
options: a:The effects of both the alcohol and the drug may be increased.,b:Nothing will happen.,c:The effects of both may be reduced.
note: Combining alcohol with medications or other drugs can amplify impairing effects, increasing danger to the driver.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Where is passing not permitted?
options: a:On a hill or curve where you cannot see ahead.,b:When a school bus is stopped and its lights are flashing.,c:When approaching an intersection.
