note: Never pass on hills or curves with limited visibility, at intersections, or where signs or markings prohibit passing; never pass a stopped school bus with flashing red lights.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Where is parking prohibited?
options: a:On a crosswalk or in a marked bicycle lane.,b:On a hill.,c:In a parking lot.
note: It's illegal to park on crosswalks or within marked bicycle lanes; when parking on the street, be within 12 inches of the curb.

question: When moving from the left lane into the right lane, you should:
options: a:Check your mirrors, signal, and look over both shoulders for other vehicles before changing lanes.,b:Check your mirrors, signal, and look over your left shoulder for other vehicles before changing lanes.,c:Check your mirrors, signal, and look over your right shoulder for other vehicles before changing lanes.
note: Before changing lanes, check mirrors, signal, and look over the shoulder on the side you intend to move into to verify your blind spot is clear.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: The space you need to cross traffic depends on:
options: a:The presence of a stop sign.,b:The use of your turn signals.,c:Road conditions, weather conditions, and oncoming traffic.
note: The gap needed to cross or turn depends on road and weather conditions, vehicle speed, and how much oncoming traffic there is.

question: Which statement about driving on wet roads is true?
options: a:As you drive faster, your tires are less effective at clearing water and hydroplaning risk increases.,b:Good tires eliminate any risk from water.,c:Deep water is less dangerous than shallow water.
note: Higher speeds reduce tire traction on wet roads and can cause hydroplaning; reduce speed and increase following distance in wet conditions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which of the following statements about passing is true?
options: a:Use your mirrors and look over your left shoulder to check your blind spot when passing to the left.,b:When passing, wait until you can see both headlights of the passed car in your rearview mirror before returning to your original lane.,c:Signal at least 100 feet before changing lanes to pass and ensure there is no oncoming traffic.
note: When passing, signal well in advance, check mirrors and your blind spot, and return to your lane only when you can see the passed vehicle’s headlights in your rearview mirror.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When changing lanes, which practice is especially important?
options: a:Signal your intentions in advance.,b:Check your blind spot by glancing over your shoulder.,c:Make sure the lane is clear before moving.
note: While signaling and ensuring the lane is clear are important, checking the blind spot by looking over your shoulder is essential to avoid hidden vehicles.

question: When you hear a fire engine siren behind you, what must you do?
options: a:Slow down until it passes you.,b:Drive with your flashers on.,c:Pull over to the side of the road and stop.
note: Upon hearing an emergency vehicle siren, safely pull to the curb or side and stop to allow the emergency vehicle to pass.

question: If you hear a siren behind you while driving, what is the correct response?
options: a:Pull over to the right and stop to allow the emergency vehicle through.,b:Stop where you are and wait.,c:Speed up to get out of the way.
note: Create a clear path by pulling to the right and stopping; if traffic prevents pulling over immediately, keep moving slowly until you can.

question: If you hear or see an approaching emergency vehicle on a divided multilane highway, you should:
options: a:Stop as quickly as you can.,b:Slow down, move your vehicle to provide a clear path for the emergency vehicle, and stop.,c:Disregard the signal if there are other lanes available for the emergency vehicle.
note: Yield to emergency vehicles by slowing and moving out of their way when it is safe; do not try to outrun them.

question: Which of the following is true about work zones?
options: a:They may be stationary or involve moving operations and are marked with orange signs.,b:They are marked only by black and white signs.,c:They never require drivers to slow down or pay extra attention.
note: Work zones can be stationary or moving (e.g., mowing, striping) and are identified by orange signs; drivers must slow down and be alert.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When do you have the right-of-way for a left turn?
options: a:When a green arrow pointing left is showing.,b:When a solid green light is on.,c:When a flashing yellow appears.
note: A steady green arrow pointing left gives you the right-of-way to turn left in that direction, as oncoming traffic is stopped.

question: When roads are slippery, what should you do?
options: a:Slow down.,b:Drive more quickly to get through the slippery area sooner.,c:Maintain the posted speed limit regardless of conditions.
note: Reduce speed at the first sign of rain, snow, or sleet and increase following distance; road conditions may require driving below the posted limit.

question: If the driver ahead is distracted (driving with one hand and talking), you should:
options: a:Avoid following the driver's example.,b:Give the vehicle extra space.,c:Know that the driver in the vehicle ahead is reducing their safety margin by being an inattentive driver.
note: When another driver appears distracted, increase the space between you and them to reduce collision risk.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you pass your exit on the interstate, you should:
options: a:Make a U-turn to go back to the exit.,b:Continue driving and use the next exit.,c:Quickly cut across traffic to make your turn.
note: Do not make sudden maneuvers; continue to the next exit and leave the interstate safely there.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When approaching a steady yellow traffic light, drivers should:
options: a:Accelerate to avoid a red light.,b:Continue driving, as they have the right-of-way.,c:Slow to a stop, unless they are already within the intersection.
note: A steady yellow light warns the signal will soon turn red; stop if it is safe to do so unless you are already in the intersection.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Approaching a railroad crossing you should:
options: a:Be ready to stop.,b:Look for a train.,c:Slow down.
note: When approaching any railroad crossing, slow down, look both ways for trains, and be prepared to stop if needed.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a traffic light changes from green to yellow as you approach, what is the best action?
options: a:Be prepared to stop safely; do not speed up to beat the red.,b:Speed up to make it through the intersection.,c:Brake sharply in the center of the intersection.
note: A steady yellow warns the light will soon turn red; slow and stop if you can do so safely.

question: When are road surfaces most slippery during a rainstorm?
options: a:During the first 10 to 15 minutes of rainfall.,b:After it has been raining for an hour or more.,c:The day after it rains.
note: Pavement can be especially slick during the initial minutes of rainfall because oil and residue rise to the surface, increasing skid risk.

question: If an emergency vehicle with flashing lights is approaching in your area, what is your duty?
options: a:Speed up to avoid the emergency vehicle.,b:Stop your vehicle immediately and prevent them from passing.,c:Make every effort to give the emergency vehicle a clear path of travel.
note: When you see or hear an emergency vehicle with lights or siren, safely pull to the side or otherwise clear the lane to allow the vehicle to pass.

question: How should you treat a vehicle that has just parked at the side of the road when passing it?
options: a:Assume the driver may open a door and use extra caution.,b:Speed up to pass quickly.,c:Slam on your brakes to be safe.
note: Assume parked vehicles may have occupants opening doors or pulling out; pass with caution and leave extra lateral space when possible.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a crossing guard directs traffic in a school zone, you must:
options: a:Follow the crossing guard's directions.,b:Follow what surrounding traffic does regardless of the guard.,c:Assume the guard is mistaken.
note: Obey crossing guards and be prepared to reduce speed and exercise extra caution in school zones.

question: If another driver cuts you off in traffic, what is the safest response?
options: a:Pull next to the driver and yell at them.,b:Let it go and continue driving safely.,c:Flash your high beams at the driver.
note: Avoid escalation and road rage: let it go, slow down if necessary, and resume safe driving.

question: If you hear a siren and cannot immediately see the emergency vehicle, you should:
options: a:Keep driving until you see the vehicle.,b:Slow down. Don't stop until you see it.,c:Pull to the curb and look to see if it is on your street.
note: If you hear an emergency vehicle and don’t know its location, pull over to the right, stop, and look to determine its direction before proceeding.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When may you proceed through a stop-sign-controlled intersection that has no stop line or crosswalk?
options: a:After coming to a complete stop before entering the intersection and ensuring it is safe.,b:After slowing down and checking for traffic.,c:After stopping at least 20 feet before the intersection.
note: If there is no stop line or crosswalk, stop before entering the intersection and proceed only when safe.

question: Why is night driving more difficult than daytime driving?
options: a:Visibility is reduced in the dark.,b:Cars overheat more quickly at night.,c:It is more likely to be raining at night.
note: Reduced illumination and contrast at night shrink your field of vision; drive at speeds that allow you to stop within the range of your headlights.

question: What should you avoid doing on potentially slippery roads?
options: a:Using cruise control and making sudden speed or direction changes.,b:Reducing your speed and driving carefully.,c:Keeping a large following distance.
note: On slippery surfaces avoid cruise control and sudden inputs; reduce speed and increase following distance instead.

question: Seat belts are most effective when worn by whom?
options: a:The driver only.,b:Passengers only on long drives.,c:All occupants of the vehicle at all times.
note: All occupants should wear seat belts on every trip; unbelted passengers can become projectiles in a crash and injure others.

question: To prepare for any hazards ahead on the road, you should:
options: a:Stare straight ahead at all times.,b:Drive with your left foot resting lightly on the brake pedal.,c:Continually scan the entire road and all roadsides.
note: Scan far ahead and to the sides of your vehicle, checking mirrors and surroundings to anticipate hazards.

question: When must you stop for a school bus on a two-lane highway?
options: a:Only if its lights are flashing and it's stopped to load/unload children.,b:When it is parked on the shoulder empty.,c:Whenever you see a bus approaching regardless of lights.
note: On a two-lane road, traffic in both directions must stop while a school bus displays flashing red lights and/or extends its stop arm.

question: When sharing the road with a truck, remember that trucks generally:
options: a:Require a smaller turning radius than smaller vehicles do.,b:Require longer distances to stop than smaller vehicles do.,c:Require less time to pass on a downgrade than smaller vehicles do.
note: Because of their size and weight, trucks need more room to stop and maneuver; avoid lingering in their blind spots.

question: When driving with other vehicles on the road, what is the safest general approach?
options: a:Drive with the flow of traffic while obeying the posted speed limit.,b:Drive faster than the flow of traffic to avoid conflicts.,c:Drive significantly slower than everyone else.
note: Driving with the flow of traffic, within posted limits, reduces the chance that other drivers will make risky maneuvers to pass.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When changing lanes on a highway, which sequence of actions should you take?
options: a:Signal, check mirrors, and glance over your shoulder to check blind spots.,b:Signal only — mirrors are optional.,c:Check the blind spot only after beginning the lane change.
note: Proper lane changes require signaling, checking mirrors, and a shoulder glance to ensure the blind spot is clear.

question: When near a motorcycle, you must allow it to:
options: a:Use only half a lane.,b:Use a full lane.,c:Use the shoulder while you share the lane.
note: Motorcycles are full-size vehicles and are entitled to a full lane and room to maneuver safely.

question: Lack of sleep affects driving ability similarly to which of the following?
options: a:The effects of alcohol.,b:The effects of amphetamines.,c:The effects of simple anger.
note: Fatigue can impair driving much like alcohol does; for example, being awake 18 hours can impair driving comparable to a BAC of about 0.05%.

question: What does a solid yellow arrow displayed by a traffic signal mean?
options: a:Means that drivers may turn in the direction indicated by the arrow.,b:Is never used as a traffic signal.,c:Has the same meaning as a circular yellow traffic light (prepare to stop).
note: A solid yellow arrow functions like a yellow traffic light for that turning movement: slow down and prepare for the signal to change to red.

question: Why must you use extra caution around a pedestrian carrying a white cane?
options: a:They are likely blind.,b:They are a police officer.,c:They are deaf.
note: A white cane or guide dog indicates a blind pedestrian. You must slow down, yield the right-of-way, and be prepared to stop to avoid injuring them.

question: Which recommendation does not help night driving safety?
options: a:Looking into oncoming headlights to adjust your vision.,b:Keep your windshield clean.,c:Carry a flashlight in your vehicle.
note: Avoid looking into oncoming headlights; clean windshields and a flashlight can help when driving at night.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When changing lanes or turning, what must you always do?
options: a:Signal your intention well in advance, even if no traffic is immediately visible.,b:Only signal when other vehicles are visible.,c:Signal only in daylight.
note: Always use your turn signals when changing lanes, turning, or pulling from a curb so other road users are aware of your intentions.

question: What does a solid white line between lanes indicate on a multi-lane road?
options: a:Lanes are moving in the same direction and drivers are not permitted to pass.,b:Lanes are moving in opposite directions and drivers are not permitted to pass.,c:Lanes are moving in opposite directions and drivers may pass when safe.
note: White pavement markings separate lanes moving in the same direction; a solid white line discourages or prohibits lane changes and passing.

question: What do work zone signs indicate?
options: a:Less-than-ideal driving conditions; exercise extra caution.,b:That it is summer.,c:You must stop and back up immediately.
note: Orange work zone signs warn of roadway work and changing conditions; slow down and be cautious.
